headline: Xanadu, a photonic quantum computing company, and chipmaker GlobalFoundries agreed to produce key quantum computer components on GlobalFoundries' 300 mm manufacturing line in New York.
score_reason: Real industrial manufacturing step announced by both companies, but no volumes, dates or money are stated.
importance_line: Quantum computer builders and their investors get a sign that photonic parts could be made on standard chip lines, though the companies give no output figures or timetable.
summary: Quantum Zeitgeist reports, citing a joint Xanadu and GlobalFoundries announcement, that the two companies will make parts for large quantum computers on GlobalFoundries' 300 mm production line in Malta, New York, starting with light detectors that Xanadu expects to make its machines faster. Xanadu builds quantum computers that use particles of light (photons) as qubits, and the companies say the parts are meant to support its planned error-tolerant demonstration machines; the text gives no production volumes, dates or financial terms.
notes: HPCwire page blocked (HTTP 403); read at Quantum Zeitgeist, which cites the companies' release. Statements are company claims.
